subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: Why Hybrids Fascinate Us
description: A micro-lesson that makes Why Hybrids Fascinate Us usable.

hook.text: Mermaids, griffins, gargoyles, nagas—cultures combine animals and humans obsessively. The urge is universal.

buildup.text: Hybrids represent boundary violations. They exist in two categories at once—and that terrifies and attracts us.

discovery.text: Mary Douglas argued that cultures classify the world, and things that don't fit become either sacred or taboo.

twist.text: Modern culture still creates hybrids: cyborgs, humanoid AI, modified organisms. The mythic impulse continues.

climax.text: Hybrid beasts test our categories. They ask: where does human end and animal begin? No one has answered yet.

punchline.text: Mix two things. Create a new fear.

quiz.question: According to Mary Douglas, what happens to things that don't fit cultural categories?
